name: Mental Maths: Square Numbers — Core Facts 1² to 30²
description: A KaTeX-enabled square-number deck with instant recall through 30², reverse square-root facts, next-square reconstruction, odd-difference patterns, base methods around 10/20/25/30, last-digit rules, and mixed practice.
estimatedTime: 150–190 minutes for a first focused pass; then 10–15 minute review bursts

cards.term: Square Numbers: What is a square?
cards.definition:
A square is a number multiplied by itself: n² = n × n.

$$
\begin{aligned}
12^2&=12\times12=144 \\
15^2&=15\times15=225
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Square Numbers: Why learn squares through 30²?
cards.definition: They are high-value anchors for multiplication, roots, algebra identities, approximation, and competitive-exam calculation. They also make close-product methods much faster.

cards.term: Square Numbers: What is the next-square rule?
Square Numbers: Why do consecutive squares differ by odd numbers?
cards.definition:
Because (n + 1)² − n² = 2n + 1, an odd number.

$$
\begin{aligned}
20^2-19^2 \\
&=400-361 \\
&=39
\end{aligned}
$$

Square Numbers: How do you self-check a square?
cards.definition: Estimate its size and examine the final digit. A square can end only in 0,1,4,5,6,9, never 2,3,7,8.

cards.term: Square Numbers: Which square is closest to 500?
cards.definition: 22² = 484 and 23² = 529. Therefore 22² is closer to 500.

cards.term: Square Numbers: Which square is closest to 1000?
cards.definition: 31² = 961 and 32² = 1024. Therefore 32² is closer to 1000.

cards.term: Square Numbers: Why are squares useful for products?
cards.definition:
They support (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b². Example:
$$
\begin{aligned}
48\times52 \\
&=50^2-2^2 \\
&=2496
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Which can be the last digit of a square: 2, 5, or 8?
cards.definition: Only 5. Squares can end in 0,1,4,5,6,9.

cards.term: Can a perfect square end in 3?
cards.definition: No. No integer square ends in 3.

cards.term: True or false: Every consecutive-square gap is odd.
cards.definition: True. (n + 1)² − n² = 2n + 1, which is odd.

cards.term: True or false: A square can end in 7.
cards.definition: False. Integer squares never end in 2, 3, 7, or 8.
